findings.claim: The closed-half-line C-infinity predicate is not equivalent to representation by an arbitrary finite positive measure. Its advertised unrestricted pointwise-limit closure is also false. Finite mass ensures continuity at zero, not finite derivatives of every order there.
findings.evidence: The roadmap explicitly uses ContDiffOn on Ici 0 at lines 163-164 and an iff with every finite representing measure at 178-192. At Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, CompletelyMonotone/Basic.lean:195 uses within derivatives for that strong predicate, while :483 defines IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi as continuity on Ici 0 plus complete monotonicity on Ioi 0. Bernstein/HausdorffBernsteinWidder.lean:70 proves the unique-representation iff for the latter. Laplace/Representation.lean:504 requires all moments for the strong converse; :517 defines RepresentsLaplace. Counterexample: mu=sum(n>=1) 2^(-n) delta_(2^n) has mass 1, but its Laplace transform has infinite negative right derivative at zero. Also exp(-n t) converges on [0,infinity) to the discontinuous indicator of {0}.
findings.fix: In Part B and its Bernstein milestone, import IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi and hausdorff_bernstein_widder_existsUnique for the finite-measure iff. Retain the stronger closed-smooth predicate separately with iteratedDerivWithin and the all-moments sufficient converse. State pointwise-limit closure on the open half-line with a finite-valued limit; the continuous-at-zero variant additionally requires continuity of the limit there. Add the infinite-first-moment and exp(-n t) endpoint regression examples. Do not rebuild the existing representation theorem.

findings.claim: The common proof paragraph wrongly says the Yosida approximants generate contraction semigroups for both general (M,omega) Hille-Yosida and Lumer-Phillips. The general-growth case does not have this property in the original norm.
findings.evidence: Roadmap lines 129-131 apply the contraction assertion to both milestones. For A=I on R, M=1 and omega=1, R(lambda,A)=(lambda-1)^(-1) I and A_lambda=lambda/(lambda-1) I for lambda>1. Its positive-time exponential has norm greater than 1. At Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, Semigroups/Generation/HilleYosida/Approximation.lean:105 gives a bound by M under exponent-zero power estimates, and Shift.lean:49 supplies the A-omega I reduction. Engel-Nagel, One-Parameter Semigroups, II.3.5 and II.3.8, printed pp.73-78, distinguish contraction generation from general growth.
findings.fix: Split the proof contracts: use contractive Yosida exponentials for the contraction hypotheses; for general growth use the existing shift reduction, the exponent-zero uniform M estimate, convergence and shift back (or an explicitly justified equivalent norm). Update the stale build-here sentence to import the pinned generation construction. Add A=I as a regression distinguishing the two regimes. Keep PDE and OT consumers on the existing general semigroup interface.

findings.claim: The bound norm(F a)<=Re(F 0) and continuity-at-zero implies uniform continuity are not valid for positive-definite functions on an arbitrary involutive additive monoid. They silently import the group-negation specialization into the BCR time monoid.
findings.evidence: The generic monoid scope is explicit at roadmap lines 200-208 and the unqualified conclusions at 211-213. On nonnegative reals with identity involution, F(t)=exp(t) is positive definite since its finite quadratic form is the squared modulus of sum_i c_i exp(t_i). It is continuous at zero, unbounded and not uniformly continuous. At Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, PositiveDefinite/Basic.lean:206 has the general diagonal Cauchy-Schwarz bound; :213 assumes a+star(a)=0 for the bound by F(0). PositiveDefinite/Continuity.lean:250 assumes a seminormed additive group and star(x)=-x for uniform continuity.
findings.fix: Keep the general monoid definition and diagonal Cauchy-Schwarz API. Restrict the bound by F(0) to a+star(a)=0, and the cited uniform-continuity theorem to the group-negation setting. Retain boundedness as an independent BCR hypothesis; import the existing qualified declarations. Add exp(t) on the identity-involution time monoid as a negative test. Carry this distinction into graph-gluing and kernel consumers.

findings.claim: The strict Hausdorff-dimension threshold dim_H(A)<n-1 does not imply uniqueness of a Wasserstein barycenter. The roadmap follows an older Agueh-Carlier draft; the revised manuscript uses the non-strict threshold.
findings.evidence: Roadmap lines 1379-1382 explicitly require only sets of dimension less than n-1. Agueh-Carlier, Barycenters in the Wasserstein space, Definition 3.2 p.10, December 10, 2010 author manuscript, says "less than or equal to d − 1"; Proposition 3.5 p.11 uses that predicate. The August 17, 2010 draft has the older strict inequality. In R^2, the uniform laws on perpendicular centred line segments both kill all Borel sets of dimension <1. Every coupling has squared transport cost 2/3. Coupling equal parameters or opposite parameters gives distinct midpoint laws on the two diagonal segments, each an equal-weight barycenter. Full calculation and version hashes are in the report.
findings.fix: Change the predicate in OT Layer 12 item 7 and its stage description to nullity of every Borel set with Hausdorff dimension at most n-1, citing the revised Definition 3.2 and Proposition 3.5. Propagate this predicate to the uniqueness and multi-map assertions. Keep absolute-continuity and L-infinity conclusions at their separate stronger tiers. Add the perpendicular-segment example rejecting the strict-threshold variant. This repairs an outdated target, not a newly discovered error in the revised source.

findings.claim: Möbius reduction handles lines and circles, but cannot straighten a general regular real-analytic arc. The L4 proof route needs a local biholomorphic chart for that case.
findings.evidence: Roadmap line 120 says "across an analytic arc / circle by Möbius reduction". A Möbius preimage of the real axis is a generalized circle, whereas the regular real-analytic parabola t+i t^2 lies on no line or circle on any interval. At Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, Complex/Conformal/Reflection/Arc.lean:160, differentiableOn_chartedSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric, uses holomorphic open partial homeomorphisms for source and target charts, conjugation-invariant chart domains, continuity, one-sided holomorphy and the real-boundary condition. It does not require those charts to be Möbius transformations.
findings.fix: State Möbius reduction only for lines/circles. For a general regular analytic arc, use a local biholomorphic straightening chart and the existing charted-reflection theorem, keeping its source/target and boundary hypotheses. Add a parabolic-arc example using the local inverse of z+i z^2 near zero. Update the prose and extracted L4 description without rebuilding reflection or changing its reviewed built verdict.
